review_candidates.title: Senior Program Officer, Global Health Agencies and Funds, Multilateral Development Banks (11-months LTE*)
review_candidates.description: The Foundation We are the largest nonprofit fighting poverty, disease, and inequity around the world. Founded on a simple premise: people everywhere, regardless of identity or circumstances, should have the chance to live healthy, productive lives. We believe our employees should reflect the rich diversity of the global populations we aim to serve. We provide an exceptional benefits package to employees and their families which include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with no premiums, generous paid time off, paid family leave, foundation-paid retirement contribution, regional holidays, and opportunities to engage in several employee communities. As a workplace, we’re committed to creating an environment for you to thrive both personally and professionally. The Team The Global Health Agencies and Funds (GHAF) team leads the strategic relationships and drives engagement on governance, strategy, operational effectiveness and programmatic impact with several key global health institutions (GHIs) and multilateral development banks (MDBs): WHO, the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, TB & Malaria (Global Fund), UNITAID, UNICEF, the World Bank, and the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB). Our engagement with the World Bank includes the Global Financing Facility (GFF) and broader health financing initiatives, while our engagement with the IsDB includes the Lives and Livelihoods Fund (LLF) and its emerging concessional financing platform. health-related initiatives. We Engage With Leaders Of These Institutions, Participate In Governance Through Membership On Boards And Committees And In Advisory Groups, And Make Targeted Investments To Strengthen Institutional Capabilities, Operational Effectiveness, And Programmatic Impact. While Many Teams Within The Foundation Work With These Institutions, The GHAF Team Specifically Works To Bring deep knowledge of the strategic, governance, operational and programmatic approaches of and across the GHIs to inform foundation strategies and engagements; Drive internal alignment on foundation-wide strategic priorities, objectives, outcomes, and accountabilities with these GHIs; and Increase the strategic coherence across the GHIs on priorities for the wider foundation through cross-institutional strategies, including a focus on product access, surveillance, and health financing. Application Deadline: Friday, December 11, 2026 Your Role The Senior Program Officer, Multilateral Development Banks will play a strategic and operational leadership role in managing the foundation's partnerships, investments, and governance engagements with the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB), Lives and Livelihoods Fund (LLF), and World Bank's Global Financing Facility (GFF). The role operates at the intersection of multilateral development finance, global health strategy, institutional governance, and investment management, translating foundation priorities into financing partnerships, institutional reforms, and measurable development outcomes. Success in this role requires the ability to independently manage complex institutional partnerships, influence senior multilateral partners, navigate sophisticated financing and governance arrangements, and drive alignment across multiple foundation teams and external partners. You will oversee a complex, multi-million-dollar investment portfolio and coordinate cross-foundation engagement to improve the strategic and programmatic value of these investments. This includes core contributions and complementary investments in institutional strengthening, technical assistance, project implementation, and adaptive results-based management. A central responsibility will be overseeing the Foundation's engagement with LLF, including its governance, strategic direction, investment portfolio, and efforts to strengthen IsDB's project preparation, implementation, and results management capabilities. In addition, the SPO will play a leading role in shaping the foundation's engagement with the next generation of concessional financing at IsDB, including the newly established IsDB Concessional Fund (ICF). This involves financing architecture, governance, concessionality, and operational priorities to advance shared global health and development objectives. You will also help shape and implement the foundation's strategic engagement with the GFF, including governance participation, institutional relationship management, investment oversight, and in close partnership with the GFF SPO, coordination with foundation teams to advance country-led health financing priorities. This is an 11-month limited term role with foundation benefits. Relocation will not be provided. What You’ll Do Lead the implementation of the foundation’s 2026 Engagement Strategy with the LLF in partnership with the foundation’s Europe and Middle East Office, and PSTs across the foundation Support the Foundation’s strategic engagement with IsDB and LLF, managing key relationships with institutional leadership, fund management, governance representatives, and technical counterparts, in close coordination with the Deputy Director. Translate complex MDB financing policies, programming cycles, country pipelines, and investment processes into actionable guidance for foundation leadership, PSTs, and regional teams. Advise foundation leadership on emerging opportunities, risks, institutional developments, and strategic decisions related to MDB partnerships and global health Oversee the strategic management, execution, and performance of approximately $200 million in foundation investments, including complex grants, institutional partnerships, and performance-based contracts. Develop the new Bodies of Work for LLF and results framework to manage and track GHAF’s investments and tactics. Develop governance positions, strategic recommendations, decision briefs, and senior leadership materials to advance foundation priorities and inform institutional decisions. Support internal work on cross-foundation priorities important to multilateral financing, including the design of new strategies, collaborations and implementation plans to ensure sustainability/impact. Represent the Deputy Director MDBs as needed in internal and external meetings. Engage with senior partners, clearly communicating complex programming and nuanced strategic priorities of the foundation. Consult with grantees and other partners to increase project impact and ensure grants are meeting strategy goals; this may include conducting site visits, providing operational guidance, and convening meetings of key partners. Support inclusive culture through modeling behaviors and actions; advance issues promptly to appropriate partners. Your Experience Advanced degree in public health, international development, public policy or related field. Minimum of 10 years of experience in multilateral engagement, program design and implementation. Proven experience working with the World Bank, Global Financing Facility, Islamic Development Bank, Lives and Livelihoods Fund, or similar institutions. Proven ability to engage and influence senior institutional leaders, government counterparts, donor representatives, and governance bodies in complex multilateral environments Demonstrated complex project management skills, particularly for execution planning and a successful track record of leading or running multiple projects simultaneously. Demonstrated experience managing large, complex investment portfolios and grants, including strategic planning, negotiation, financial oversight, performance management, and risk mitigation. Experience designing or overseeing institutional strengthening, technical assistance, results-based management, and monitoring and evaluation initiatives Exceptional ability to navigate ambiguity, exercise independent judgment, and translate complex institutional and financial issues into actionable strategic recommendations Strong consultative and advisory skills. Demonstrated excellence in influence and leadership, ability to build trust, be a team leader and player who motivates and educates other team members and understands the value of interpersonal relationship building. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing executive-level briefings, governance materials, strategic analyses, and investment recommendations. Comfortable in a wide range of cultural, geographic and operational situations, demonstrating culturally sensitive behavior with a diverse range of people and a deep commitment to development issues and high standards of personal integrity. Ability to operate effectively at both strategic and operational levels, connecting institutional policy and financing decisions to country-level implementation and impact Ability to travel up to 25% domestically and internationally. Must have unrestricted work authorization in the country where this position is located. The Foundation does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. This includes direct company sponsorship and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (eg: H-1B, O-1, L-1, E, OPT, STEM-OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc.). The salary range for this role is $190,100 to $294,700 USD. We recognize high-wage market differences in Seattle and Washington, D.C., where our offices are located. The range for this role in these locations is $209,100 to $324,100 USD. As a mission-driven organization, we strive to balance competitive pay with our mission. New hires salaries are typically between the range minimum and the salary range midpoint. Actual placement in the range will depend on a candidate’s job-related skills, experience, and expertise, as evaluated during the interview process. Hiring Requirements As part of our standard hiring process for new employees, employment will be contingent upon successful completion of a background check. Candidate Accommodations We’re committed to providing an inclusive and accessible hiring experience for all candidates. If you have a disability or medical condition and need an accommodation at any stage of the application or interview process—such as an ASL interpreter, alternative interview format, or physical accessibility support—we’re happy to help. Please contact HR@gatesfoundation.org with the position number and a brief description of your accommodation needs. Requests will be handled confidentially. Inclusion Statement We are dedicated to the belief that all lives have equal value. We strive for a global and cultural workplace that supports ever greater diversity, equity, and inclusion — of voices, ideas, and approaches — and we support this diversity through all our employment practices. All applicants and employees who are drawn to serve our mission will enjoy equality of opportunity and fair treatment without regard to race, color, age, religion, pregnancy, sex, sexual orientation, disability, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, and prior protected activity.

review_candidates.title: Senior Financial Analyst (Richmond, Hybrid)
review_candidates.description: Dominion Energy is committed to providing reliable, affordable, and increasingly clean energy that powers our customers every day. If you want to work for a purpose-driven company that values safety and collaboration, we’re looking for you. You won’t just find a job here; you’ll find your career. Review the position below and apply today . We offer a hybrid 3-2 work schedule (three days in the office, two days of teleworking) to accommodate the need for flexibility. Military service members and veterans with ranks from E5-E9, W1-CW5, or O3-O6, plus appropriate equivalent combination of education and years of experience as outlined below will be considered for this opportunity. At this time, Dominion Energy cannot transfer or sponsor a work visa or employment authorization for this position. Job Summary The Senior Financial Analyst supports the development, evaluation, and advancement of electric power generation projects across the Company’s diverse generation portfolio, including utility-scale solar, distributed solar, battery energy storage systems (BESS), natural gas generation, advanced nuclear technologies, and other emerging energy resources. This role provides analytical and project development support to the Generation Development team and serves as a key resource for maintaining the Company’s project development intelligence and cost tracking capabilities. This position serves as the steward of the Generation Development organization’s project portfolio information and reporting framework. The role is responsible for maintaining accurate and comprehensive financial data related to the Company’s generation development pipeline, including project scope, capital investment requirements, operating assumptions, real estate data, and other commercial terms for projects developed by the company or for potential project acquisitions. Through the development of portfolio reporting, analytics, and executive-level insights, the position supports strategic planning, resource acquisition decisions, regulatory filings, capital investment evaluations, corporate budgeting and senior leadership decision-making. The role works closely with project managers and functional subject matter experts to ensure consistency, transparency, and accountability across the Company’s development portfolio. A primary responsibility of this position is supporting resource planning and long-term strategic financial and customer value assessments by working closely with internal stakeholders to develop, collect, verify, and analyze project cost and performance assumptions used in integrated resource planning, capacity expansion modeling, regulatory filings, financial analyses, and business case evaluations. This role collaborates with teams across Generation Development, Project Construction, Strategic Planning, Finance, Power Generation Planning, and other business units to ensure consistent and reliable project financial and performance data are utilized consistently across the organization. Through effective management of project information and analytical support, this position contributes to the successful advancement of generation resources needed to meet the Company’s reliability, affordability, sustainability, and long-term growth objectives. Required Knowledge, Skills, Abilities & Experience The knowledge, skills, abilities and experiences that are required for entry into this job include the following: Experience: Minimum 5+ years of relevant experience in power generation development, utility planning, financial analysis, engineering, project controls, business analytics, energy markets, or related disciplines. Experience supporting utility-scale infrastructure or energy project development is preferred. Industry Knowledge: Some working knowledge of electric power generation technologies and project development processes, including generation planning, project development, capital budgeting, cost estimating, and financial evaluation. Familiarity with utility resource planning, regulatory proceedings, and energy market fundamentals is preferred. Analytical and Financial Expertise: Strong analytical and quantitative capabilities with the ability to organize, evaluate, and interpret large amounts of technical, financial, and operational data. Experience developing business cases, lifecycle cost analyses, economic evaluations, and investment comparisons is preferred. Data Management and Reporting: Demonstrated ability to manage and maintain large datasets and project information repositories. Experience developing processes, dashboards, reports, and data governance practices to improve the quality, accessibility, and consistency of project information across multiple stakeholders. Tools and Systems: Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and data management applications. Experience with financial modeling, database tools, business intelligence platforms, project management software, or resource planning applications is preferred. Ability to develop analyses and presentations that support executive and regulatory decision-making. Collaboration and Stakeholder Engagement: Proven ability to work effectively in a cross-functional environment and build strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders. Experience coordinating information across planning, engineering, finance, regulatory, construction, environmental, and commercial organizations is preferred. Communication Skills: Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate complex technical and financial information clearly and concisely. Experience preparing executive summaries, business reports, regulatory support materials, or analytical presentations is preferred. Strategic Thinking and Problem Solving: Ability to identify trends, evaluate alternatives, and provide well-supported recommendations. Demonstrated ability to connect project-level information with broader planning, financial, and strategic objectives. Project Management and Organization: Strong organizational and project coordination skills with the ability to manage multiple assignments, prioritize competing deadlines, and maintain high levels of accuracy and attention to detail. Ability to independently track project information and support multiple development initiatives simultaneously. Education Requirements Education Level: Bachelor preferred in Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, Economics, Engineering (Mechanical, Electrical, Civil, Industrial, Energy Systems, or related discipline), Management Information Systems (MIS), Energy Management, or a related field Licenses, Certifications, or Quals Description Working Conditions Office Work Environment 76 -100% Travel Up to 25% Other Working Conditions Test Description No Testing Required Export Control Certain positions at Dominion Energy may involve access to information and technology subject to export controls under U.S. law. Compliance with these export controls may result in Dominion Energy limiting its consideration of certain applicants. The actual salary offered may vary based on factors such as the selected candidate’s qualifications, skills, experience, and work location. This is not intended to represent the full salary range for the position or limit future compensation growth. At Dominion Energy, we offer excellent plans and programs for employees. Employees are rewarded with a competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package which includes: health, dental, and vision benefits with coverage for families and domestic partners, vacation, retirement plans including 401k contributions and matches, paid holidays, tuition reimbursement, bonus eligibility, sick leave, and disability insurance. To learn more about our benefits, click here: dombenefits.com. Dominion Energy is an equal opportunity employer. review_candidates.title: Senior Executive Director
review_candidates.description: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. Application deadline: Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised. BACKGROUND The International Rescue Committee (IRC) helps people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC is at work today in over 40 countries and 28 U.S. cities. The IRC’s Resettlement, Asylum and Integration (RAI) department creates opportunities for refugees and other vulnerable migrants to survive and thrive in the US and Europe. RAI serves more than 100,000 individuals each year in the US, including newly arrived refugees and asylum seekers as well as the broader immigrant community, through a diverse portfolio of programs aimed at five core outcomes: Health, Safety, Economic Wellbeing, Education and Power. SCOPE OF WORK The Senior Executive Director (SED) provides dynamic leadership for the delivery of high-quality programs within their assigned portfolio (“cluster”) of program offices. The SED directly leads the Atlanta, Miami, and Iowa City program offices and provides leadership, oversight, and support to additional offices within the cluster. They develop a vision for the assigned cluster to achieve impact, growth, operational compliance and excellence, and fiscal sustainability and effectively engage with IRC teams, partners, and external parties to bring the vision to life. Most office clusters will comprise between six to eight program offices and a total annual operating budget of between $26 - $40 million. Major Responsibilities Leadership Lead the development and implementation of RAI’s Strategy100 and local Strategic Action Plan (SAP) initiatives, ensuring alignment with client aspirations and organizational goals. For primary office(s), set and communicate vision and strategy. Establish and maintain strong relationships with local leaders, including the State Refugee Coordinator, and communities to further IRC’s mission and act as a thought and operational leader. Foster cooperative working relationships with state and local agencies and service providers, donors, advocacy partners, and community organizations. Mentor, advise, and support Executive Directors (EDs) and Site Directors (SDs) as they lead program offices. Support EDs in designated cluster to improve local relationships as appropriate and always enabling the designated ED/SD to be lead in their communities. Program & Operational Oversight Ensure efficiency of own primary program office, while also providing support and building high performance in other offices within the assigned portfolio. Coordinate cluster operations, ensuring high-quality service delivery in both union and non-union environments and under emergency conditions and/or drastically changing geopolitical landscapes. Empower local leadership to ensure that programs are developed collaboratively with strong programmatic cohesion across sectors, particularly between resettlement and non-resettlement programs. Provide strategic and operational support to EDs, reinforcing their leadership without assuming representational responsibilities on their behalf within their office and/or community. Lead goal setting, track work progress, and assess outcomes to meet departmental objectives and employee needs. Engage with RAI and Support Function leaders to drive systems solutions that improve organizational efficiency. Promote innovative programming within the cluster and work collaboratively to pilot new ideas. Financial & Grants Management Ensure good stewardship of IRC and donor resources. Exercise oversight of operating budgets and cultivate a diligent approach to fiscal management, ensuring that the program offices within the cluster fully meet their obligations. Fundraising & Business Development Develop and communicate strategic fundraising priorities which articulate IRC’s vision and ability to provide tangible solutions to specific societal problems. Drive vision for office resource development and provide strategic oversight and mentoring to leaders, business development, and grants management teams to meet targets. Ensure significant efforts are dedicated to locally sourced public funding, beyond ORR pass-through, in addition to private fundraising. Public Advocacy & Media Relations Communicate the organization’s mission, impact, and client needs to various audiences. Advocate for humanitarian issues and promote policy changes at the local and national levels. Lead local advocacy efforts in home office and support cluster and national advocacy efforts; host Board, senior staff, and donor visits, and engage in and support community and policy outreach efforts. Manage IRC's public image; partner with local media; collaborate with IRC Communications team. Foster positive relationships with all collaborators, including client communities, local and regional employers, healthcare providers, school systems, and civil service. Work with partners to enable client success. Cultural Sensitivity and Supportive Supervision Cultivate an inclusive, accountable culture rooted in IRC’s People Manager Standards and Guiding Principles. Lead a diverse team of staff, interns, and volunteers within the cluster, supporting high performance and well-being. Manage cluster functions per IRC policies and standards, encouraging a safe work environment for staff and clients. Engage on staff development, retention, and succession planning that fosters an engaging, diverse, and equitable environment. KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS Position reports to: Vice President, Program Delivery Position directly supervises various positions including: the highest-ranking leader at each program office within their cluster, and the leadership team of the Sr. ED’s home offices. Key partners : RAI HQ Units and IRC Shared Services Support functions groups including Operations, Finance, Strategy, Policy & Advocacy, and People & Culture. Key Competencies & Qualifications Critical personal characteristics The ideal candidate is a strategist and thought partner who will see beyond their immediate team, role, and cluster and collaborate across functional groups to implement action plans that support broader organizational goals and a ‘One IRC culture.’ As a manager, they will engage, rally, and inspire the team to the highest quality of work. As a leader, they will engage positively with counterparts and leadership at the headquarters level and work towards a constructive and progressive environment. Demonstrated Skills And Proficiencies Ability to coordinate, plan, schedule, determine priorities and meet deadlines. Outstanding written and verbal communication skills are essential. Ability to anticipate and assess situations accurately and recommend/implement effective courses of action required. Ability to coordinate multiple meeting tasks and a myriad of complex details on a concurrent basis. Ability to communicate effectively with internal and external collaborators with tact and diplomacy, both orally and in writing, including working with all staff levels and diverse personalities. Ability to exercise discretion in dealing with sensitive material and maintain confidentiality. Ability to handle stress, function effectively under pressure and meet time parameters. Ability to expand on own initiative in performance of duties. Must have excellent discretion, judgment, tact, initiative, creativity, critical thinking, problem solving, organizational skills, and self-motivation. Education & Experience Undergraduate degree or equivalent experience required. Graduate degree in a relevant area strongly preferred. Minimum of 10 years’ relevant experience, including 8+ years in senior leadership roles. Experience managing large, diverse teams and multi-million-dollar portfolios in humanitarian and/or nonprofit sectors. Experience managing multi-site budgets and teams strongly preferred. WORKING ENVIRONMENT Occasional flexibility, after-hour demands and the ability to attend evening and weekend events, when needed. This position has been designated as ‘hybrid.’ It requires in-person work, including regular onsite presence within the assigned primary office(s) and periodic travel to additional office(s) within the cluster and other IRC sites. A private, secure, and distraction-free home workspace is required when not working onsite. Compensation: (Pay Rate: $162,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements. US Benefits effective Jan 1, 2027: IRC offers a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-30 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $187 per month, dental starting at $7.70 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare, dependent care, and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles. Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. review_candidates.description: ­Led by an experienced management team and supported by a strong investor group, including large and experienced institutions and strategic partners, EdgeConneX offers a dynamic, fast-paced work environment where we are bringing flexibility, proximity, power, and connectivity to some of the world’s key businesses. With major offices in Herndon, Denver, Amsterdam, Singapore and Malaysia, we have a global footprint and a unified team of employees committed to providing a premier customer experience and delivering the full spectrum of data center solutions, from core to edge, like no other data center provider can do. Focused on driving innovation and helping our customers define and deliver their own unique vision for the Edge, at any scale, in any market worldwide, for any requirement, we are building tomorrow’s data center infrastructure, today for some of the world’s most demanding Network, Content, and Cloud customers. EdgeConneX is seeking a technically accomplished, delivery-oriented mechanical engineer to serve as Senior Data Center Design Engineer for EMEA within the Global Design & Engineering (GD&E) organization. This role is the senior regional mechanical authority, accountable for the integrity of mechanical design and equipment validation across a portfolio of assigned campuses. The role also serves as GD&E's designated mechanical engineering interface across the broader EdgeConneX organization. GD&E delivers safe, reliable, and cost-effective data center infrastructure by setting world-class design standards, driving disciplined program execution, and partnering seamlessly with internal teams and an external execution partner. Within GD&E, the Senior Mechanical Engineer sits within the EMEA regional pillar and is supported by the Principal Mechanical Engineer in Technical Strategy & Architecture, who owns the global mechanical architecture and standards. The Senior Data Center Design Engineer ensures that this architecture becomes validated, commissioned, critical infrastructure in the field. The ideal candidate is first and foremost a mechanical engineer with data center or critical-infrastructure experience and practical expertise in HVAC systems, including both air and liquid cooling technologies. Key Responsibilities Serve as the senior mechanical discipline authority across the portfolio of assigned campuses in EMEA, ensuring that mechanical designs and installations conform to the standards, guidelines, and templates established by Global Technical Strategy & Architecture. Engage at the milestones where deep HVAC expertise matters most, including design reviews, submittal and RFI resolution for critical mechanical scope, factory acceptance tests (FAT), and commissioning-readiness assessments. Hold the technical position on mechanical readiness by validating that systems are ready before each phase proceeds, while supporting the TPM/DM site team rather than working in parallel with it. Identify where site-specific constraints or customer requirements require a departure from the global standard, and route deviations through the established Technical Strategy & Architecture approval process. Provide informal technical leadership and mentoring to regional SMEs, improving the consistency and rigor of design reviews across the EMEA portfolio. Review and challenge mechanical engineering deliverables produced by the execution partner, including equipment specifications, design parameters, HVAC and piping designs, control narratives, and CFD analyses, for conformance with GD&E standards and sound engineering practice. Validate that customer-specific mechanical requirements are correctly captured in the design and reconciled with the EdgeConneX standard, escalating conflicts through the deviation process rather than resolving them informally. Feed field and commissioning lessons learned back to the Principal Mechanical Engineer so that the global mechanical standard improves with every campus delivered. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or similar required; master's degree preferred. Professional engineering credentials and relevant data center certifications, such as CDCP or ATD (Accredited Tier Designer), are valued. Experience Minimum 10 years of progressive mechanical engineering experience in data centers or mission-critical infrastructure, spanning design, construction support, and commissioning, with a track record of owning mechanical outcomes on delivered facilities. Demonstrated experience on hyperscale or Tier III+ data center projects, including hands-on involvement in design reviews, factory acceptance testing, commissioning, and readiness assessments. Meaningful experience with liquid-cooling technologies and large-scale chilled-water cooling systems. Familiar with the typical electrical equipment in a data center like generators, MV-transformers electrical distribution and UPS-Systems. Experience working with or alongside execution-partner engineering teams, driving quality and standards of adherence through influence within an integrated team. Solid understanding of commissioning methodology for mechanical systems, from individual equipment startup and functional testing through Integrated Systems Testing (IST), including readiness criteria and failure-mode validation. Clear, concise communication, with the credibility to make a ‘not ready’ call on a mechanical system or commissioning plan and support it with evidence and a recovery path. Sound field judgment, including knowing when to resolve an issue directly, when to engage the Principal Mechanical Engineer, and when to escalate through the TPM/DM site team. Travel Significant travel required (25–40%) across assigned campuses in EMEA and vendor facilities for factory acceptance testing, concentrated around design reviews, equipment validation, and commissioning windows, sometimes on short notice.
